subject: Re: Acme MAP - E2E Latency Sprint & Close Milestone
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Yates <samantha.yates@acmecorp.com>, Ben Torres <ops@acmecorp.com>
Cc: qa-leads@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme MAP kickoff: E2E latency sprint proposal and tentative close milestone

Hi Samantha / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our discussion, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the performance validation you requested: an E2E latency/throughput/TTFT sprint across US, EU, and APAC with explicit failover/routing checks.

High-level proposal (attached: acme-map-v1.xlsx):
- Deliverable 1: Latency sprint (regional) — measure median/p95/p99 RTTs, cold vs warmed TTFT, and throughput at target concurrencies
- Deliverable 2: Multi-region routing & failover tests — confirm graceful fallback to lower-capacity variants and cross-region failover within specified SLOs
- Deliverable 3: Results pack + recommended configuration for Dedicated vs Hosted routing policy to meet your latency SLAs

Suggested timeline (tentative):
- May 18–19: US targeted runs (US-east, US-west windows)
- May 20: EU runs (CEST-friendly window)
- May 21: APAC runs (APAC evening window for your team)
- May 24: Delivery of consolidated results + go/no-go for close and SOW sign-off

Acceptance criteria we propose to validate during the sprint:
- TTFT < 200ms median for text-completion baseline (warm cache), p95 < 450ms
- Sustained token/sec throughput at 20 qps for profile A (see sheet: concurrency_profiles)
- Failover: < 2s for routing detection + fallback invocation in simulated region outage

Next steps: please confirm the proposed regional windows (and timezones) and whether your QA team can provide a representative prompt suite and example request sizes. I’ve cc'd your QA list so they can weigh in.

Attachments: acme-map-v1.xlsx (MAP + milestones)

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com

1) We will provide the prompt suite and an anonymized request trace by EOD Friday (May 14). QA will also include 2 long-context scenarios that typically hit our tail latencies.
2) APAC window: we prefer May 21 in the early morning SGT (08:00–12:00) if that works for you.
3) For the failover test, can you confirm whether Redwood will run both the simulated region outage and the fallback variant in production-like infra (not a dev sandbox)? We need fidelity to our routing layers.

Finally, procurement has a standard SOW template — we’ll need to review any discounts tied to committed QPS before exec sign-off.

Samantha

Samantha — thanks for the quick note. A few answers inline plus an updated schedule and run plan attached (latency-test-scripts.tar.gz contains harness + runner configs).

- Prompt suite: perfect, we’ll map the anonymized trace to our concurrency profiles. Please include the two long-context cases; we’ll earmark them for tail-latency analysis.
- APAC window: May 21 08:00–12:00 SGT works for our infra ops team; we’ll shift engineers earlier to cover warmup.
- Failover fidelity: we will run failover in a pre-production cluster mirroring your production routing (routing tables & weights) — we will coordinate a narrow maintenance window with your ops team so the test simulates an instance/region outage without impacting live traffic. This is the same approach we validated with a previous enterprise customer.

Updated milestone highlights (see attached MAP):
- May 18–19: US runs (warm/cold TTFT sweep, concurrency ramp to target)
- May 20: EU runs (include cross-region latency check from EU->US)
- May 21: APAC runs + failover drills (APAC outage simulation + fallback to EU
- May 24: Consolidated results pack and recommendation; if OK, we’ll hand off SOW for signature

Acceptance criteria refined:
- Warm TTFT median < 200ms, p95 < 450ms; cold TTFT documented for each region
- Sustained throughput at target QPS without >1% error rate for profile A
- Failover detection window < 2s; end-to-end failover stabilization < 5s

I’ve attached the latency scripts and an updated MAP. Dev, can you confirm the test harness and any ops prerequisites?

Attachments: latency-test-scripts.tar.gz, acme-map-v1.xlsx

Best,
Stephanie

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Acme MAP kickoff: Test harness & measurement details

Stephanie / Samantha —

Quick technical breakdown of how we’ll run the sprint and measure the KPIs (details below + scripts referenced in latency-test-scripts.tar.gz):

Test harness and measurement methodology:
- Warmup: 5 minutes at 50% of target QPS before each region run; this pre-populates KV cache to capture warm TTFT behavior.
- TTFT measurement: instrument client-side measured TTFT at first token received and also server-side timing; we’ll report both and reconcile differences in the results pack.
- Concurrency profiles: three profiles (A: 20 qps sustained, B: 50 qps bursty, C: 100 qps short-burst) — see concurrency_profiles.csv in the scripts tar.
- Throughput & tokens/sec: measured over 60s steady windows; we’ll include token/sec and token/error breakdowns.
- Failover: we’ll simulate region-level route withdrawal and observe routing controller+client behavior. Observables: detection latency, fallback invocation time, error spike, post-failover stabilization period.

Important ops prerequisites for Acme team:
- Short maintenance window where routing weight changes are allowed (we will not modify live routing without ops approval).
- An account-level API key with a testing scope; we’ll use per-run ephemeral keys and return all keys after the sweep.

Metric outputs we will deliver:
- CSV with per-run timings (token-level and request-level), aggregated p50/p95/p99, and a consolidated report with suggested config changes (quantization profiles, batch sizes, routing policy tweaks).

If you approve, I’ll kick off a dry-run in our staging cluster on May 16 to validate harness and warm-up behavior.

—Dev
Principal Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwoodinference.com
